title: The circle in a magnetic field
spoken: In a transverse magnetic field the circular radius is gamma m v over charge magnitude B.
explanation: In a uniform magnetic field across its motion the electron goes round a circle. Its radius is gamma m v over |q| B: larger than m v over |q| B, the value without gamma, by gamma. At 0.6c that is 25 per cent.
assumptions: An electron accelerated from rest, then moving at speed v with |v| < c. In section 10 the electron is momentarily at rest in the moving system, so its speed is that system's speed v.
Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, |q| the size of the electron's charge, U the size of the voltage.
A uniform magnetic field of strength B at right angles to the electron's velocity, in the laboratory.

notes.title: Gamma m v
notes.explanation: The quantity the field has to turn round. Without gamma this is the low-speed m v.

notes.title: Charge times field
notes.explanation: How strongly the field turns the electron.

notes.title: The ratio
notes.explanation: Metres: kilograms times metres per second, over coulombs times teslas.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: A prediction that deflection experiments on fast electrons can test: the radius grows with gamma, not with v alone.

notes.title: Size of the electron's charge
notes.explanation: The elementary charge. The sign of the charge decides the direction of the force, not these magnitudes.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: Of the electron's speed: one over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared.

notes.title: Magnetic field
notes.explanation: Across the motion, in the laboratory.

notes.title: Radius of the circle
notes.explanation: The radius of the electron's circular path in the laboratory.

notes.title: Electron speed
notes.explanation: The speed of the system in which the electron is momentarily at rest, which is the electron's own speed.
